title: Untangling Bad Habits: A Systematic Solution
coreMove: Diagnose a stubborn habit by mapping which prompt, ability, or motivation lever is feeding it, then disrupt the smallest, easiest link in that chain first

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse who scrolls Instagram for forty minutes the moment she sits in her parked car after a hard shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a healthcare worker decompressing between work and home
exampleSpecs.stakes: arriving home depleted to two kids who get the leftover version of her
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she traces the prompt back to the click of the seatbelt unlatching, not to the phone itself, and realizes the lever to pull is the prompt, not her resolve

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school band director who pours a second glass of wine while grading marching show footage on weeknights
exampleSpecs.audience: a mid-career educator with a long evening workload
exampleSpecs.stakes: showing up foggy to 7:15am rehearsals and snapping at the drumline
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he reconstructs the chain — laptop opens, footage loads, hand reaches for the bottle — and decides the cheapest cut is moving the bottle out of the kitchen, not gritting through the craving

exampleSpecs.domain: a city bus mechanic who eats a full sleeve of vending-machine cookies during his 2am break
exampleSpecs.stakes: a creeping prediabetes diagnosis his doctor flagged last month
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he picks one tiny disruption — bringing a banana and parking three steps farther from the vending machine — and accepts that the craving is a prompt problem, not a willpower problem

exampleSpecs.domain: a reference librarian who refreshes her ex's LinkedIn profile every time she opens a new browser tab
exampleSpecs.audience: a recently divorced woman in her late forties
exampleSpecs.stakes: reopening grief every workday and losing focus on patron requests
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: in conversation with a friend she lists every link in the chain — new tab, muscle-memory keystrokes, autocomplete — and chooses to change her browser homepage rather than promise herself she'll stop looking

exampleSpecs.domain: a ceramics studio owner who checks her sales dashboard fourteen times an evening
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-business owner whose income depends on the numbers
exampleSpecs.stakes: ruining dinner with her partner and sleeping badly because of a number she cannot change at 9pm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she imagines three alternative versions of the same evening, each disrupting a different lever (prompt, ability, motivation), and notices the prompt-level fix is the only one she'd actually do tomorrow

exampleSpecs.domain: a long-haul trucker who lights a cigarette every time he pulls into a rest stop
exampleSpecs.audience: a driver who has quit and relapsed four times
exampleSpecs.stakes: a chronic cough his wife is starting to flinch at
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he separates the three habits braided together — the stop, the stretch, the smoke — and picks the easiest braid to untangle first instead of trying to quit smoking head-on
